note: Everything this project has looked at, whether or not it found anything. A search that returns nothing is a result, and an archive that records only its successes will send the next person down the same dead ends. «Blocked» means a bot check or a login wall that this project has deliberately not tried to get round. «Pending» means known, wanted, and not yet obtained.
cols: What it gave, or did not

rows.what: Full-text search for the surname and for «Memorie autobiografiche»
rows.got: Carlo's «Memorie autobiografiche» (1926, 309 pp.), Salata's «Un precursore» (1929), and the 1928 bronze-bust volume with his letters to Kandler. Three works this project had recorded as unheld, all open access. Should have been searched months earlier.

Fourteen distinct articles. Already held: Jelinčić's three-part Kobler correspondence, the 2024 Arhivski vjesnik inventory, Marin on the Zagreb library. New: Kero & Bobanović on the Zadar notary Tommaso de Franceschi; two reviews of the 2023 Croatian translation of Camillo's «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino»; and a 2022 article on the Zagreb collection.

rows.what: The society's published guide and archive inventories
rows.got: «Archivio Camillo De Franceschi e famiglia», 26 boxes, 19th–20th century. The 2017 guide and the full 39-page inventory, both downloaded. A second complete family archive, distinct from Zagreb's.

rows.what: Repeated sweeps on every spelling of the surname and on the place-names
rows.got: Kobler's «Memorie» entire; Cavalli 1845 on the bishops of Pola; the Atti of Rovigno; the Wagna camp intake lists; «Il Piccolo» of Trieste for 1926; the Zagreb almanacs; the Almanacco Fiumano. The single most productive source this project has.

rows.what: Surname search across the digitised Austrian press
rows.got: The press notices of Carlo's death in January 1893, and other notices. Images retrievable from the IIIF endpoint even where the presentation manifest fails.

rows.what: Record search by surname and by place, and the parish register films
rows.got: The bulk of this archive's individual records. Deep paging caps at about offset 1,100, which limits large sweeps.

rows.src: Državni arhiv u Pazinu — microfilm ZM34K-215
rows.what: The Gallignana baptism book 1667–1745, read image by image
rows.got: Five occurrences of the surname in seventy-eight years, and a systematic negative for the rest. The most labour-intensive single piece of work here and the one that answered the central question.

rows.what: Surname search across the digitised Australian press
rows.got: Australian notices for the family's later generations.
The 1949 sailing and the word «apatride».
The USAT General Stewart, Naples to Melbourne, April 1949, passengers 0180–0182.

rows.what: The Kobler and Carlo De Franceschi pages, and the bibliography of his works
rows.got: The complete bibliography of Carlo's published writings, which is what led to the «Memorie autobiografiche». Also a clean transcription of chapters of «L'Istria» (1879). The site's firewall refuses plain command-line requests and needs an ordinary browser.

One sentence naming the Benzoni and the De Franceschi among Fiume's immigrant merchants. Checked against Kobler and found to be a compression: right on the Cremonese Benzoni, loose on the Bono, and it reverses the direction of travel for the De Franceschi. Cited as a lead, not as authority.

rows.what: The complete text layer of the Catholic Historical Review, Nova et Vetera and The Thomist — 496 issues, 236 MB
rows.got: Zero occurrences of any spelling of the surname connected to this family, and zero for all twenty place-names. Every «De Franceschi» in five gigabytes of theology is a French historian of Jansenism, a Sienese printer, or a Venetian chancery secretary. The one thing worth keeping was a pointer to Orbanić's 1788 Pićan visitation.
One footnote citing Sylvio Hermann De Franceschi, a living French historian. Nothing else.
A Bologna anthropologist of the Argentine Gran Chaco. The surname is the author's own and there is no connection to this family.
Concerns Andrea de' Franceschi, Venetian grand chancellor, of Cividale di Belluno — a different family. Useful only as a caution about how many unrelated houses carry this name.
Concerns Francesco De Franceschi, printer, «born in Siena around 1530». A third unrelated family.

Excellent background on the sixteenth-century Pazin frontier and a useful Istrian place-name gazetteer, but every «De Franceschi» in it is a citation of Carlo or Camillo as authors. Six Gologorica marriages in the Boljun register 1585–1608, none of this surname — consistent with a later arrival.

rows.src: Corsican records — RHFC register index, 226 communes
rows.what: Every commune, births, marriages and deaths, letter D
rows.got: Four Defranceschi baptisms at Tomino in Cap Corse 1843–56, and a second cluster at Levie and Sartène in the far south. 132 Defranceschi births in the whole of France 1891–1990. Nothing whatever connects them to this family, and the honest position is that these are unrelated houses sharing a patronymic.
HTTP 403 on every URL, including the public surname pages. Not circumvented.

rows.what: Civil registration for Carnia and the Veneto
rows.got: Bot check. Not circumvented. This is the route to the Ovaro civil registers and it remains closed to automated access.
Refused. The wanted article was found open access elsewhere.
Bot check. Not circumvented.

rows.src: Mémoire des Hommes, Grand Mémorial, Base Léonore
rows.got: JavaScript applications with no reachable interface. Not searched.

De Buset's parish-by-parish visitation of the Pićan diocese, 31 March – 31 August 1788, 178 sheets, published Vatican City 2016. Covers Gologorica and Gallignana. The manuscripts are in the Diocesan Archives of TRIESTE, not Pazin.

rows.src: «Stemmi della nobiltà di Buccari», Bakarski zbornik 2 (1996)
rows.got: Fifty-seven pages on the arms of Bakar's patrician houses.

rows.src: Bertoša, «Pisma Carla De Franceschija Šimi Ljubiću», VHARP 13 (1968)
rows.got: Carlo's letters to Šime Ljubić, printed. The archive knew of five in the Zadar state archive and did not know they were in print.
A summary of the whole published Kobler correspondence.

rows.src: Gentileo, «Bibliografia degli scritti di Camillo De Franceschi», AMSI 55 (1954)
rows.got: Camillo's full published bibliography.

rows.src: Camillo de Franceschi, «Povijest Pazinske knežije na temelju isprava» (Pazin 2023)
rows.got: The 2023 Croatian translation of «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino», 574 pp., translated by Klara Buršić Matijašić and Robert Matijašić. In print and purchasable.

rows.src: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Notarile antico B. 2979
rows.got: Franceschi Gio. Batta, notary at Mione, protocols 1737–1783. Needs a letter, not a search box.

rows.src: Državni arhiv u Rijeci, HR-DARI-382 kut. 1
rows.got: The 1896 «Albero genealogico della Famiglia de Franceschi», said to reach back into the fifteenth century.
A series this project has never opened, and the family's own recollection points at it.

rows.src: Vergé-Franceschi, «Le cap Corse: généalogies et destins» (2006)
rows.got: The reference work for Cap Corse families; would settle whether the Tomino Defranceschi are in it.

rows.what: Surname and place searches across the digitised Croatian press, including the Bakar papers Galeb and Kvarner
rows.got: In progress. An ASP.NET search that will not answer a plain command-line request and has to be driven like a person. It carries two Bakar newspapers, which is the sharpest reason to work it.

rows.src: Camillo de Franceschi, «Povijest Pazinske knežije» — reviews
rows.got: The two Croatian reviews of the 2023 translation both state that the family «se iz talijanske pokrajine Karnije doselila u Gologoricu u 16. stoljeću» — moved from the Italian province of Carnia to Gologorica in the sixteenth century. The first published source this archive has seen that names Carnia rather than Friuli, and it gives a fourth date for the migration.

rows.src: Kero & Bobanović on the Zadar notary Tommaso de Franceschi (2023)
rows.got: A notary of the surname at Zadar whose ninth fascicle holds an unusually large number of unpublished Glagolitic documents from Biograd. Not yet shown to connect to this family; recorded because a notary of the name in Dalmatia is worth knowing about.

rows.what: Read in full, both language columns
rows.got: The Agrons castle, the investitures of 1467 and 1471, the 1502 «gismanus de Carnia», the de Franciscus at Mione in the 16th century, the 1661 first mention as «mistro Zuanne», the 1686 death of the «vecchio stipite», the 1712 imprisonment of the parish priest, and the eighteenth-century professions. The single richest page found this year.

rows.what: 9,000 pages crawled for the surname and for eight place-names
rows.got: 319 pages carry the name; 250-odd are bare citations of Carlo or Camillo as authors. The rest include the encyclopedia entry, Brhan's Carnic-emigration study with the Mione emigrant register, the 1945 census by place, the Umag cemetery survey, a Francesco de Franceschi bishop of Pola 1422–26, and Dionigi Defranceschi of Gallignana in the Dachau index.

rows.src: Ferigo, «Le cifre, le anime» — full text
rows.got: Confirms what this archive already published from it, and supplies the join it had missed: the 1679 weavers' return lists «Agrons e Cella» and «Mione» as neighbouring entries, and the family held the castle at the one and lived in the other.

rows.src: Camillo De Franceschi, «Storia documentata della Contea di Pisino», AMSI 1963 vols 10–12
rows.got: The authority the Istarska enciklopedija cites for the Agrons charters. 516 pages. Republished in Croatian translation at Pazin in 2023. The highest-value unheld book after the Memorie.
A Croatian translation of the Memorie autobiografiche, made by Istrian scholars; will carry an apparatus the 1926 edition does not.
Contains «Gologorički De Franceschi: između etosa i etnosa», the footnoted scholarly version of the encyclopedia entry.
